summary: A UK Radiators blog how-to explaining the two main ways to control radiator temperature: thermostatic radiator valves (TRVs) and smart radiator valves. It describes how TRVs shut off hot water to a single radiator once the room reaches the set temperature, including a frost prevention mode, and how smart valves learn occupancy patterns via motion sensors. The page is mostly promotional, with boilerplate navigation, product ads and related-post links removed.
one_line: Explains how thermostatic and smart radiator valves control room temperature, and where TRVs should not be installed.
key_facts: The article says there are two ways to control radiator temperature: thermostatic radiator valves (also known as TRVs) and a smart thermostat that can control radiators individually.
Thermostatic radiator valves use mechanisms, sometimes using liquid or wax, that shut off the flow of hot water to a specific radiator when the room temperature reaches the desired level.
Thermostatic radiator valves do not interact with the boiler directly but heat radiators quicker by shutting off the water supply earlier.
The article states that TRVs mean the boiler switches off quicker, saving money, reducing the carbon footprint and reaching the desired comfort level.
Good thermostatic radiator valves have a frost prevention mode that detects when room temperature drops below a certain level and reopens the valve slightly.
The frost prevention mode is said to prevent radiators and pipes from freezing, becoming damaged and potentially bursting.
The article advises that TRVs shouldn't be installed in bathrooms, due to frequent temperature changes, or in rooms where the boiler thermostat is located.
Smart radiator valves can replace the heads of thermostatic radiator valves and use motion sensors to detect people in the space.
A smart radiator valve learns the times of day the user needs the room to be warm and turns the valve on and off accordingly.
The temperature the room should be at is still set by the user with smart radiator valves.
To have the ultimate control, the article says a full set of heating controls is needed, including a smart thermostat panel and a set of smart radiator thermostats.
The article's example smart thermostat product is the Salus iT600 Smart Home Smart Thermostat VS20WRF.
The example TRV product shown is the Talus Flair - White Thermostatic Radiator Valve.
The page directs readers to The Ultimate Guide to Radiator Valves for more on their choices.
The seller UK Radiators is based at Unit C, Caxton Court, Newcomen Way, Severalls Industrial Park, Colchester, CO4 9TG.
